posts.subject: Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 Webcam
posts.author: mjeshurun
posts.message_html:
Hi friends, 

I recently ordered a Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 monitor. 

When I received the monitor I tried to install and lock the webcam according to the instructions in the user manual, but I found that the webcam's locking screw is turning indefinitely and doesn't actually screw into the designated screw hole on the monitor.
So it basically doesn't lock on the monitor.

From a photo I took of the webcam, it looks like I received a unit with a broken webcam locking screw. 

Since it was supposed to be a completely new monitor, I decided to return the monitor to the store and asked for a replacement unit, but the second monitor came with a similar issue, and its webcam also doesn't screw into the monitor -- contrary to the way the user manual suggests it should. 

Has anyone else encountered a similar issue?

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 Webcam
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello and welcome to the Lenovo Community mjeshurun,

And thank you for describing the issue so clearly. I understand how frustrating it is when the detachable webcam of your Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 will not secure properly, especially after seeing the same behavior on two replacement units.

Based on what you described, a few quick checks may help confirm whether this is a fit/alignment issue or a hardware problem:

1. Remove the webcam and inspect both the screw and the threaded mounting point on the monitor for any visible misalignment, cross-threading, looseness, or obstruction.
2. Re-seat the webcam carefully so it sits fully flush before turning the locking screw. If the screw spins freely without any resistance, the threads may not be engaging. Please check chapter 1-10 of its User Guide here for additional reference.
3. Try tightening only with light finger pressure and do not force the screw, as forcing it may damage the threads.

Let us know how it goes.

Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 Webcam
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Thanks for getting back to us mjeshurun,

What you are describing sounds more like an installation/alignment issue than a broken screw, especially since it happened on two new units.

Please try this in order:

1. Remove the webcam completely and inspect the mounting area on the monitor and the webcam attachment point. Make sure there is no protective film, packing material, or insert blocking the mount.
2. Position the webcam exactly as shown in the setup guide and seat it fully before turning the locking screw. The screw usually will not extend or catch correctly unless the webcam is properly aligned in the mounting slot first.
3. When tightening, turn the screw gently clockwise only after the webcam is sitting flush. Do not force it with a screwdriver at first.
4. If it still does not catch, back it off completely, reseat the webcam, and try again while applying light inward pressure so the threads can engage.
5. If the screw spins freely even when the webcam is correctly seated, avoid forcing it further with a screwdriver, as that can damage the mount.

Since you already saw the same behavior on two units, the most practical next step is to have the seller or technical support physically verify the webcam mounting method as they can confirm whether the webcam module or mount is faulty. If possible, ask them to test with another webcam from the same model in front of you. You can contact the technical support at 1-809-456-979 and their operating hours are 8:00 -18:00 Sunday - Thursday.

Best regards,
Adriel_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 Webcam
posts.author: Adriel_lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hello again mjeshurun,

Since the same webcam locking screw behaved the same way on two brand-new units, and you already tested it both on the monitor and off the monitor with a screwdriver, this is no longer a normal setup issue. If the screw turns continuously without extending or engaging, the webcam locking mechanism is most likely defective.

At this point, the right next step is to return or exchange the monitor again rather than continue troubleshooting.

When the next unit is opened, ask the store to test the webcam locking mechanism before you leave: first confirm the screw visibly moves in and out when turned, then attach the webcam to the monitor and verify it tightens securely.

If a third unit shows the same behavior, contact technical support directly and request a warranty case for the webcam/monitor attachment issue.

Configurations can vary between systems, but the screw should not spin endlessly without locking.

Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:Lenovo Yoga Pro 27UD-10 Webcam
posts.author: mjeshurun
posts.message_html:
A different salesman figured out what the problem was.
The webcam's security screw has to be pressed downward while screwing, because there is a spring holding it inside the webcam's body.
Once the screw is pressed down, it will then be possible to attach it to the monitor. 
Thank you for your assistance, Adriel 🙏
